Simulation: Two Latent Orderings

Ziang Zhang

Question and design

Can structural CAVI separate features that follow two different orderings of the same samples? The generator from the MPCurver feature-partitioning article creates 500 samples, ten quadratic features following ordering A, and ten monotone features following ordering B. Gaussian noise has standard deviation 0.05. The generator seed is 1.

We fit a fixed \(M=2\) model with a second-order random-walk prior, \(K=50\) grid positions, ridge = 0, and Fiedler ordering initialization. The assignment probabilities are estimated jointly with conditional feature trajectories and sample positions.

Feature assignments

After aligning the arbitrary A/B labels, the fit assigns all 20 of 20 features to their generating groups.

Figure 1. Posterior assignment probabilities for the 20 simulated features. Axis labels show the generating feature group.

Sample orderings

After aligning ordering labels and allowing reversal of each axis, the absolute Spearman correlations with the two generating positions are 0.9975 and 0.9989.

Figure 2. True versus inferred sample position for each aligned ordering. Reversing an axis leaves its ordering unchanged.

Structural objective

Figure 3. Structural variational objective within the final temperature-one phase.

The structural objective increases during the final \(T=1\) refinement phase.

Reproduce

Run the experiment script from the InferOrder root with MPCurver 0.3.0. The saved results include the generating truth, fitted model, and assignment probabilities. This is one simulated data set.
